scope: Development experiment with an optically coded non-anatomical test sheet, not comparable to unmarked validation as acceptance evidence.
material_coordinate: Render four flush bands on the existing mesh, with known longitudinal boundaries at material rows 0, 3, 6, 9 and 13. Leave nodes, springs, contact, and the trace definition unchanged. Read adjacent color transitions and depth-backed external silhouettes in the same RGB-D frame. Require the full ordered pattern on both banks of the cut, with multiple supporting pixel pairs at every boundary. Never use simulated node positions, a chord-length prior, or a remembered chart for visual control. Piecewise linear interpolation models local longitudinal stretch; excessive cross-bank disagreement or an unobservable row invalidates the chart. Report bank support and boundary locations.
control: Use the verified near boundary only with current near-edge tissue evidence for a pre-cut front. After a closure require a fresh, tissue-supported slit in the same frame as the chart with material progress at least half of the existing 0.5 mm bin beyond the pre-closure visual front. Use the nominal chart for progress and command distance, and each band's earlier across-bank 10th-percentile boundary for the sweep guard. Keep the existing sweep reserve, move limits, collision limits, recovery budgets, and 9-10 mm truth acceptance.
trials: Verify a marked truth-mode nominal control run against the historical node trace and capture marked RGB-D at the already registered optical diagnostic pose (+4.5 degrees yaw, 0 pitch, 0.080 m insertion). Use scoring-only node positions to verify both ends and quantify boundary error. Run marked vision nominal and 0.5 mm depth noise (noise seed 1) from that same optical pose. Report missing evidence, closure count, reacquisition and true cutting outcomes; no requalification of the pose, no holdout reuse, and no claims of M5 acceptance.
